We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis. The hints: step1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. Retrosynthetic: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step2: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with decarboxylation). So forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. Retrosynthetic: break the C=C and carboxyl to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step3: sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthetic: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Thus we can propose:

Target T: p-tolyl-SO2-Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (actually the aniline is attached to amide nitrogen). The amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide is formed between the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) and an aniline (aniline). So step1: disconnect amide to give cinnamic acid (or its precursor) and aniline.

But the cinnamic acid is part of the unsaturated chain attached to phenyl sulfonyl group. Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl via the phenyl ring (the phenyl bearing sulfonyl). The α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to that phenyl at the para position? Let's examine SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have to parse: c1ccc( ... )cc1 with a methyl at position 1 (C). The substituent is NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonamide attaches to the tolyl ring via N (sulfonamide nitrogen). The sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). That second phenyl has a substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N at para position (maybe). So the unsaturated amide is attached to that phenyl.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Step 1 (amide formation): disconnect the amide between C(=O) and N of aniline. Precursors: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl-sulfonyl (i.e., (E)-4-(phenylsulfonyl) cinnamic acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So product of step1: unsaturated acid + aniline.

Step 2 (Doebner modification): The unsaturated acid can be derived from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl-sulfonyl benzaldehyde) and malonic acid. So break the C=C and carboxyl to give aldehyde (the phenyl-sulfonyl benzaldehyde) and malonic acid.

Step 3 (sulfonamide formation): The aldehyde precursor (phenyl-sulfonyl benzaldehyde) can be derived from sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and the aromatic amine (the phenyl ring that becomes the benzaldehyde? Wait the sulfonyl chloride attaches to the tolyl amine? Actually the sulfonamide is between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl-sulfonyl? Let's examine: The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (p-tolyl). The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring. So the sulfonamide formation is between p-toluidine (the amine) and phenylsulfonyl chloride (the sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic: break S-N bond to give p-toluidine and phenylsulfonyl chloride (which is attached to the second phenyl ring). The phenylsulfonyl chloride is derived from chlorosulfonic acid on the second phenyl? Actually phenylsulfonyl chloride is a sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl. So we can propose that the sulfonyl chloride is commercially available.

Thus final route:

1. Amide coupling: (E)-4-(phenylsulfonyl) cinnamic acid + aniline -> target.

2. Doebner modification: phenylsulfonyl benzaldehyde + malonic acid -> (E)-4-(phenylsulfonyl) cinnamic acid.

3. Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + phenylsulfonyl chloride -> phenylsulfonyl benzaldehyde? Wait the sulfonyl chloride attaches to p-toluidine to give sulfonamide, but we need phenylsulfonyl benzaldehyde (i.e., the phenyl ring bearing sulfonyl group and aldehyde). Actually the sulfonamide formation step is between p-toluidine (amine) and phenylsulfonyl chloride to give p-tolyl-NH-SO2-Ph (the sulfonamide). But the aldehyde is on the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl group. So the phenylsulfonyl chloride must already have the aldehyde substituent? No, the aldehyde is on the phenyl ring that is attached to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride must be 4-formyl phenylsulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride). That would give after sulfonamide formation: p-tolyl-NH-SO2-4-formylphenyl. Then Doebner modification uses that aldehyde (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl) with malonic acid to give the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl-sulfonyl. Yes.

Thus step3: p-toluidine + 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride -> p-tolyl-NH-SO2-4-formylphenyl (the sulfonamide aldehyde). This is the precursor for step2.

Thus we need to ensure the aldehyde is para to sulfonyl group. In target, the sulfonyl is attached at para position relative to the unsaturated chain? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. The sulfonyl attached to phenyl at position 1, and the unsaturated chain at para position (position 4). So indeed the aldehyde would be at para position before Doebner.

Thus route is consistent.
